construction.clear_header: v, workspace_id, credential_id, epoch, gen, seq, nonce[12], digest
construction.sealed_body: LP("done/env-body/v1") || LP(actor_id) || LP(actor_kind) || u32be(count) || ( u32be(len) || update )*
construction.aad: LP("done/env/v1") || LP(dec v) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(credential_id) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(dec gen) || LP(dec seq)
construction.signature: Ed25519 over LP("done/env-sig/v1") || LP(dec v) || LP(workspace_id) || LP(credential_id) || LP(dec epoch) || LP(dec gen) || LP(dec seq) || LP(hex nonce) || LP(hex digest)
construction.digest: SHA-256(ciphertext) — validated by the relay without a content key (§7.2)
construction.nonce: 12 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues() per envelope, under a 2^32-per-generation budget that `seq` already bounds — row 3’s argument, unchanged
construction.seq: The credential’s own monotonic position. The service’s accepted position must equal it, which is what makes row 5’s chain gap-free by construction rather than by assertion
construction.batching: One envelope carries one actor. A batch closes at a change of actor, credential, epoch or generation; at a flush interval that must not be shorter than the acceptance-head cadence, since the envelope waits for a head regardless (§7.5); or at a byte cap. The interval and cap are tunables with grounds, not constants with authority
construction.length_prefix: uint16be(byteLength) || utf8 for text; uint32be for update bytes

not_here.primitives: AES-256-GCM, HKDF, SHA-256 and Ed25519 KATs are row 1’s, in test/vectors/algorithm-suite.json.
not_here.acceptance: The link and head that travel beside an envelope are row 5’s, in test/vectors/finalization.json.
not_here.retention: How deep a device retains its own outbound envelopes is row 6.

device.role: The device signing credential (§13.4). Signs; never receives a content key for signing alone.

other_credential.role: A different admitted credential. Present so "signed by another credential" is a vector rather than a sentence.

vectors.name: single-update
vectors.why: One 18-byte Yjs update — the measured size of a keystroke — from a human actor. The common case.

vectors.name: batched-updates
vectors.why: Three updates from the same actor, credential, epoch and generation, in one envelope. §7.4 permits exactly this batching and no other.

vectors.name: system-actor
vectors.why: An import, attributed to the system actor (§9.2). The actor is a sealed field, so its kind is invisible to the relay.

vectors.name: rotated-generation
vectors.why: The same bytes under generation 2. `gen` selects which K_g the subkey comes from, so it is bound in both lists.

must_fail.name: aad-only-label
must_fail.mutate: The label is where this carrier authenticates its own version, so a renumbered envelope must fail to open rather than select another suite (row 1).

must_fail.name: aad-only-v
must_fail.mutate: Claim format version 2 for bytes sealed as version 1.

must_fail.name: aad-only-workspace_id
must_fail.mutate: Open the envelope as though it belonged to another workspace, subkey unchanged. This is the AAD half of §11.2 test 3’s cross-workspace replay; the subkey half is `wrong-workspace-subkey`.

must_fail.name: aad-only-credential_id
must_fail.mutate: Attribute the envelope to another credential. The credential is what the epoch binds capabilities to, so this is where §11.2 test 3’s capability change lands.

must_fail.name: aad-only-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Move the envelope to a later epoch — the field §7.5 shows cannot by itself distinguish accepted from withheld, and which therefore must at least be immovable.

must_fail.name: aad-only-gen
must_fail.mutate: Claim a content-key generation the envelope was not sealed under.

must_fail.name: aad-only-seq
must_fail.mutate: Renumber the envelope’s position. Row 5’s accepted chain binds this position, so a movable `seq` would move a link.

must_fail.name: sig-only-label
must_fail.mutate: Verify under a renumbered signature label.

must_fail.name: sig-only-v
must_fail.mutate: Verify as though the header claimed format version 2.

must_fail.name: sig-only-workspace_id
must_fail.mutate: Verify against another workspace id.

must_fail.name: sig-only-credential_id
must_fail.mutate: Verify as another credential’s envelope.

must_fail.name: sig-only-epoch
must_fail.mutate: Verify against a later epoch.

must_fail.name: sig-only-gen
must_fail.mutate: Verify against another generation.

must_fail.name: sig-only-seq
must_fail.mutate: Verify against another position.

must_fail.name: sig-only-nonce
must_fail.mutate: Verify against a different nonce. **The AAD structurally cannot bind this**, so the signature is the only thing that does.

must_fail.name: sig-only-digest
must_fail.mutate: Verify against a different ciphertext digest. **The AAD structurally cannot bind this either** — it is a function of the ciphertext the AAD helped produce — so a substituted body is caught here or nowhere.

must_fail.name: wrong-workspace-subkey
must_fail.mutate: Derive K_net for another workspace and open with it. Tests the HKDF info binding; the AAD half is `aad-only-workspace_id`.

must_fail.name: signed-by-other-credential
must_fail.mutate: A well-formed signature over the correct message, produced by a different admitted credential. §7.4 forbids re-signing another credential’s operations, and this is the check that notices.

must_fail.name: flipped-tag-bit
must_fail.mutate: Flip the low bit of the final tag byte.

must_fail.name: truncated-ciphertext
must_fail.mutate: Drop the final byte of the ciphertext.

must_fail.name: digest-not-of-ciphertext
must_fail.mutate: A header whose `digest` is not SHA-256 of the ciphertext beside it. The relay validates this without a content key (§7.2), so it is refused before any client sees it.
